---
title: "Get started"
description: >
  Build the smallest complete bslibreact app: a Python Shiny server and a
  React client that looks like a bslib page.
---

This article builds the smallest complete bslibreact app. The Shiny server is
written in Python and does the reactive work. The page is a React client that
shows a slider in a sidebar, a value box, and a plot, all with bslib's own
markup and styling.

![The finished app: a sidebar with a slider, a value box showing the
slider's value, and a histogram.](https://www.samuelbharti.com/bslibreact/assets/hello-py.png)

## Requirements

- Python 3.10 or newer.
- A current Node.js LTS release, to build the client.
- git, to copy the example.

## 1. Install the Python packages

```bash
pip install bslibreact shinyreact matplotlib numpy
```

`bslibreact` brings Shiny for Python with it. `shinyreact` provides the page
and the plumbing between Shiny and React. matplotlib and numpy are only for
this example's plot.

## 2. Copy the example app

The repository holds this app as `examples/01-hello`. Clone the repository
and copy that folder:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/samuelbharti/bslibreact.git
cp -R bslibreact/examples/01-hello myapp
cd myapp
```

The folder has two halves:

| File | Role |
| --- | --- |
| `app.py` | The Shiny server. It holds reactive code only. |
| `src/App.tsx` | The React client. It lays out the page. |
| `src/ui.tsx` | Mounts `App` on the page. It is the same in every app. |
| `vite.config.ts` | Builds `src/` into `www/ui.js`. |
| `www/ui.js` | The built client that the server sends to the browser. |

`app.R` is the same server in R. Delete it if the app only needs Python.

## 3. Read the server

`app.py` has no layout code. Its page is shinyreact's `page_react()`, and
`page_deps()` gives that page the CSS and JavaScript a bslib page would
attach on its own.

```python
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np
from bslibreact import host_input, page_deps
from shiny import App, render, ui
from shinyreact import page_react

app_theme = ui.Theme()

app_ui = page_react(
    page_deps(app_theme),
    title="Hello bslibreact",
    theme=app_theme,
)
```

The server function then does three things.

```python
def server(input, output, session):
    host_input(output, "bins", lambda: ui.input_slider("bins", "Bins", 1, 50, 30))

    @render.plot
    def plot():
        bins = input.bins()
        fig, ax = plt.subplots()
        ax.hist(np.random.normal(size=500), bins=bins, color="#447099", edgecolor="white")
        return fig

    @render.text
    def bins_count():
        return str(input.bins())


app = App(app_ui, server)
```

`host_input()` renders a real `ui.input_slider()` on the server and hosts it
for the client to display, so the slider keeps the look and behaviour Shiny
gives it. The client mounts it under the id `bins_ui`, and the server reads
its value as `input.bins()`, as in any Shiny app.

`plot` and `bins_count` are ordinary Shiny outputs. A hosted slider has no
value until the client has mounted it. Until then `input.bins()` stops the
output silently, so both stay blank and then fill in. `plot()` reads the
input before it opens a figure, so no figure is left open in the meantime.

## 4. Read the client

`src/App.tsx` is the whole page. Each component reproduces the markup of one
bslib or Shiny call.

```tsx
import {
  PageSidebar,
  SliderInput,
  PlotOutput,
  ValueBox,
  TextOutput,
  useShinyInitialized,
} from "bslibreact";

export default function App() {
  const ready = useShinyInitialized();
  if (!ready) return null;

  return (
    <PageSidebar title="Hello bslibreact" sidebar={<SliderInput id="bins_ui" />}>
      <ValueBox title="Bins">
        <TextOutput id="bins_count" className="value-box-value" />
      </ValueBox>
      <PlotOutput id="plot" height="400px" />
    </PageSidebar>
  );
}
```

The ids connect the two halves:

| Client | Server |
| --- | --- |
| `<SliderInput id="bins_ui" />` | `host_input(output, "bins", lambda: ui.input_slider("bins", ...))` |
| `<PlotOutput id="plot" />` | `@render.plot def plot()` |
| `<TextOutput id="bins_count" />` | `@render.text def bins_count()` |

A hosted input always carries the `_ui` suffix on the client. `bins` is the
slider's own input id, so the element that hosts it needs a different one.

## 5. Build the client

```bash
npm install
npm run build
```

`npm install` fetches the `bslibreact` npm package, and the build writes
`www/ui.js`. While developing, `npm run dev` rebuilds on every change to
`src/`.

## 6. Run the app

```bash
shiny run app.py
```

Open the address it prints. The page matches the screenshot above. Move the
slider, and the value box and the histogram both update.
